validity: INVALID as a test of the engine: the audit holds 3 decisions of 20. The controller process stopped after minute 3 (its log is in the run artifact, which this lab cannot download); a single failed kubectl call ended the loop. For the remaining 17 minutes the cluster held Omni's last settings (4 workers, HPA target 77%, pod CPU limits at 69.5%) with no engine running.
significance: no metric significant (2-minute blocks, bootstrap 95%): node-hours per core-hour -18.1% [-2.77,+0.28]; kWh per core-hour +18.2% [-0.03,+0.31]
rbac: all can receipts yes (HPA, cordon, eviction, pod resize, deployment, security ConfigMap); all cannot receipts no (delete nodes/pods/deployments, create pods, load generator, kube-system, secrets, namespaces, write security ConfigMap)
kill_switch: restored target 50; workers 6 of 6; pod CPU limits 500m; no Omni records left
reading: The faster response times are real measurements but are not evidence for the engine: the engine was not running for most of the run, the two arms ran on different CI machines, and a capped static configuration answering faster than native points at machine-to-machine noise. Nothing is significant.
fix: controller fail-safe (a failed decision is recorded and skipped; 3 in a row restore native settings and stop); the benchmark now prints the controller log and rejects a run with fewer than 80% of decisions
